title: Sales Enablement: Positioning, Competitive Briefs, Pitch Decks, Pricing & Security FAQ
author: Asha Patel
body:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook centralizes Redwood Inference's go-to-market assets for technical and enterprise sales motions: core positioning and messaging, short competitive briefs for field use, pitch deck recommended flow, pricing guidance and talk tracks, representative case studies, and a prospect-facing Security FAQ. Use this as the canonical source for sales collateral and for preparing deal briefs and demos.

Audience: AEs, Sales Engineers, Solutions Architects, Field Marketing, and Partner/Channel teams.

Owner & maintenance
- Document owner: go-to-market (Asha Patel)
- Review cadence: quarterly (update after major product, pricing, or SLAs changes)
- Approval: Sales leadership + Product marketing for messaging changes

1) Positioning and core messaging (elevator + value props)

Elevator (30s): Redwood Inference is a developer-first inference platform that delivers predictable, production-grade LLM inference across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments, so engineering teams get consistent latency, cost-efficiency, and operational control without building a custom serving stack.

Three core value props (customer-facing bullets):
- Production-grade performance: predictable latency and throughput (SLO playbooks and Dedicated capacity) that make LLMs viable for interactive, high-concurrency applications.
- Unified deployment options: same API and operational tooling across hosted, reserved (Dedicated), and private (VPC / on-prem) deployments to meet security and compliance needs.
- Cost & quality controls: batching, caching, and quantization recommendations plus per-route cost dashboards to reduce unit economics while maintaining output quality.

Messaging pillars and proof points
- Reliability & SLAs: Highlight Dedicated contracts with committed GPU pools and 99.9% uptime targets; describe multi-tier fallback (model variants and region routing).
- Developer productivity: SDKs, quickstarts, and example integrations (Node/Python) with streaming and function-calling examples.
- Observability & ops: per-route latency/cost dashboards, token-level attribution, and tracing hooks that map model regressions to prompt sets.
- Enterprise readiness: KMS/HSM integrations, audit logs, RBAC, and VPC deployment options.

2) Competitive brief (one-page for field use)

Competitor at-a-glance (short summaries and battle cards):
- OpenAI (hosted API)
  - Strengths: broad model capability, large ecosystem, fast TTV for prototypes.
  - Weaknesses: limited private deployment options; pricing can be opaque at scale; fewer controls for dedicated capacity and granular infrastructure routing.
  - Win themes vs OpenAI: predictable unit economics, private deployment & data isolation, Dedicated reserved capacity with SLAs.

- Anthropic
  - Strengths: safety-first models and clear research branding.
  - Weaknesses: fewer ops features for enterprise rollout and less focus on multi-deployment serving parity.
  - Win themes: Ops & reliability features, unifying hosted/dedicated/private experience, advanced cost controls.

- AWS Bedrock / Google Vertex AI
  - Strengths: deep cloud integration, procurement familiarity for enterprises.
  - Weaknesses: less prescriptive inference runtime optimizations for serving LLMs (per-token economics), variable performance across models, potential vendor lock-in.
  - Win themes: Best-in-class inference performance, transparent per-route cost attribution, flexible deployment outside a single cloud.

- Self-hosted inference vendors (open-source runtimes + infra partners)
  - Strengths: maximum control and potentially lower TCO at very large scale.
  - Weaknesses: long build time, ops burden, lack of fully-featured control plane and observability.
  - Win themes: Faster time-to-value, out-of-the-box observability, SLAs and managed options for Dedicated.

Competitive objections & rebuttals (quick bullets)
- Objection: "We can just self-host and save money."
  - Rebuttal: Self-hosted can reduce sticker but increases engineering cost and time-to-market. Redwood bundles runtime optimizations (batching, KV caching) and cost tooling that typically reduces total cost of ownership for product teams.
- Objection: "We already use cloud AI provider X for models."
  - Rebuttal: Redwood complements model providers; our platform standardizes serving and ops across providers and can run compatible model variants with routing/fallback for reliability and cost control.

3) Recommended pitch deck flow (15-20 slides)

Slide checklist (minimal recommended slide titles):
1. Title / Customer-focused value statement
2. Pain: Why inference is the hard part (latency, cost, reliability)
3. Opportunity: LLM use cases that require production-grade serving
4. Redwood intro: one-liner + product modes (hosted / Dedicated / Private)
5. How it works: runtime + smart routing + caching/batching (diagram)
6. Developer experience: API, SDKs, quickstarts, demo link
7. Performance & cost: representative benchmarks and per-token cost examples
8. Security & compliance: VPC, KMS/HSM, audit logging
9. SLAs & operational model: Dedicated commitments, support tiers, escalation path
10. Pricing summary: reference tiers and guidance (see section 4)
11. Case study / customer proof (one of the examples below)
12. Deployment & onboarding plan: PoC / Pilot steps and timeline
13. Next steps & CTA (trial, pilot, partner SE assignment)

Tips for the field:
- Tailor the early slides to the buyer persona: emphasize infra & TCO for platform owners; emphasize developer velocity and SLAs for product/engineering leaders.
- Always include a one-slide technical diagram of the runtime and traffic flow for SE-led conversations.

4) Pricing guidance & talk tracks

Pricing principles (for AEs):
- Flexible billing modes: usage-based for Hosted, committed monthly/annual for Dedicated, and enterprise licensing for Private.
- Pricing should highlight predicted unit economics: tokens/second throughput vs price per million tokens and cost-saving levers (batching/caching/quantization).
- Offer a pilot program (timeboxed) to validate latency/cost targets before committing to Dedicated.

Reference pricing talk-track (illustrative only; negotiate based on ARR and deployment model):
- Hosted (self-serve): metered per-token pricing with free trial credits; volume discounts at thresholds (e.g., 10% off > $50k/mo).
- Dedicated: committed GPU capacity with monthly minimums; base price + overage model; enterprise SLA and priority support.
- Private (on-prem/VPC): platform license + optional managed services; professional services for deployment and day-2 ops.

Sample price comparison table (example numbers for field use; replace with current quotes):
| Mode      | Billing model           | Typical contract size | Notes |
|-----------|-------------------------|-----------------------|-------|
| Hosted    | Per-token (metered)     | $0 - $50k / month     | Fast TTV, self-serve |
| Dedicated | Committed monthly/yr    | $50k - $500k / month  | SLA-backed, predictable throughput |
| Private   | License + services      | $200k+ / year         | For regulated / air-gapped customers |

Discounting & approvals:
- Discounting follows the standard commercial discount grid. Any exceptions or multi-cloud deployment pricing should be escalated to sales ops.

5) Case studies and proof points (briefs ready for slides)

Case study: FinTech real-time chat (anonymized)
- Problem: Interactive customer support required sub-200ms median latency and PCI-compliant private deployment.
- Solution: Deployed Redwood Private with Dedicated routing for peak periods and prefix caching for common prompts.
- Results:
  - 60% reduction in average per-token cost vs prior managed endpoint after batching and caching optimizations
  - 190ms median response latency at 120 concurrent users
  - Audit logs and KMS integration satisfied compliance requirements for PCI scope reduction

Case study: Marketplace content generation
- Problem: High volume of short-generation requests causing high per-request overhead and inconsistent latency.
- Solution: Hosted + Redis-backed KV cache for prompt prefixes and automatic batching.
- Results:
  - 45% cost reduction on monthly inference bill
  - 2x improvement in throughput during peak windows
  - Faster release cycles due to integrated SDKs and CI templates

6) Security FAQ for prospects (concise Q/A suitable for inclusion in RFP responses)

Q: Where is customer data stored and how long is it retained?
A: By default, hosted customers' inference metadata required for billing is retained for 30 days. For Dedicated and Private deployments, customers control retention policies and can opt for zero-retention modes. All retention policies are configurable and documented in our data residency playbook.

Q: Do you use customer data to train models?
A: No. Redwood does not use customer data to train or improve shared model weights. Customers can opt into data-sharing programs under explicit contracts; otherwise, data is isolated and not used for training.

Q: What encryption standards do you support?
A: TLS 1.2+ in transit, AES-256 at rest. For Dedicated and Private customers we support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM).

Q: How do you handle key management and secret rotation?
A: We integrate with AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and common HSM providers. We support automatic rotation and provide audit trails for key access.

Q: Can you run in our VPC / on-prem environment?
A: Yes. Redwood Private supports VPC-hosted control planes and an on-prem turnkey package for air-gapped environments. Deployment options and required network peering are documented in the private deployment reference architecture.

Q: What compliance certifications do you hold?
A: Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II attestation and provides evidence for customer audits. For regulated customers we offer additional contractual clauses and evidence packages; reference the compliance-evidence page for details.

Q: What is the incident response and disclosure process?
A: We adhere to the incident response playbook with defined SLAs for notification. Customers in Dedicated and Private tiers receive prioritized incident communication and optionally a post-incident technical review.

7) Sales playbook: pilot -> production checklist (operational steps)

Pilot (2-6 weeks recommended):
1. Scope goals: latency SLO, throughput, and cost targets.
2. Technical kickoff: SE + customer infra + sample traffic profile.
3. Run benchmark: representative dataset, peak concurrency test, and quality checks.
4. Tune: batching, cache policies, and quantization recommendations.
5. Acceptance: meet agreed SLOs and finalize Dedicated or Private contract terms.

Production rollout checklist:
- Create routing and fallback policies for peak/training scenarios
- Configure observability dashboards and alerting (token-level cost, tail latency, error rates)
- Establish runbook and on-call escalation path with SRE (if Dedicated)
- Document data retention and key-management arrangements
